name: Barbell Back Squat
summary: A foundational lower-body compound exercise where a barbell is supported across the upper back while descending into a full squat.

setup: Set the barbell in a rack at approximately mid-chest height.
Step under the bar, resting it across your upper trapezius muscles, and grip the bar firmly with both hands outside your shoulders.
Unrack the bar by extending your hips and knees, take two to three deliberate steps back, and set your feet roughly shoulder-width apart with toes slightly turned out.
steps: Inhale deeply into your abdomen and brace your core firmly.
Initiate the descent by bending at your hips and knees simultaneously, keeping your chest proud and your knees tracking in line with your toes.
Descend smoothly until your hip crease dips below the top of your knees.
Drive through your mid-foot to stand back up, keeping your torso rigid and extending your hips and knees together until you return to the starting position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale and brace your core at the top before descending, hold your breath through the bottom sticking point, and exhale forcefully once past the midpoint of the ascent.

common_faults.fault: Knees caving inward (knee valgus) during the ascent.
common_faults.correction: Actively push your knees outward so they track directly over your middle toes throughout the entire rep.

common_faults.fault: Excessive forward lean causing the hips to rise faster than the chest (stripper squat).
common_faults.correction: Maintain strong upper back tension and think about pushing your shoulders back into the bar as you reverse out of the hole.
Lower the weight if necessary and descend until your hip crease drops below the top of your patella while maintaining lumbar control.

precautions: Ensure rack safety pins are set just below your bottom squat depth.
Do not allow the lumbar spine to excessively round into flexion under load.
